boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 40:1 opens with the dateline “בְּאַרְבַּ֤ע עֶשְׂרֵה֙ שָׁנָ֔ה אַחַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכְּתָ֖ה הָעִ֑יר” (‘after the city was struck’) -- the fourteenth and last of the book's fourteen year-bearing datelines -- paired in the same verse with the hand-of-YHWH idiom “הָיְתָ֤ה עָלַי֙ יַד יְהוָ֔ה” and the transport verb “וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י שָֽׁמָּה”. This dateline-hand-transport cluster is the strongest onset class the book offers and is also a HARD seam: no row may cross it. It follows immediately, without intervening material, the utterance formula and pe that close the prior part at web:Ezek.39.29. The frame continues at 40:2 with the header “בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֔ים” ‘in the visions of God’ (one of only three such headers in the book) plus a further transport pair (“הֱבִיאַ֖נִי” / “וַיְנִיחֵ֗נִי”), and again at 40:3 (“וַיָּבֵ֨יא אוֹתִ֜י שָׁ֗מָּה”) introducing the measuring man. Close side: 40:4 carries no formula-grade close device; the seam at 40:4/40:5 rests on the man's charge, “הַגֵּ֛ד אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל” ‘declare all that you see to the house of Israel’, read as ending the entry scene before the measuring reed is put to use in 40:5's “וַיָּ֜מָד”, the first of an eighteen-verse run of that verb across 40:5-41:5. Both sides are weighed: the onset is the best-evidenced in the whole span; the close is a content judgment (charge-speech versus measuring-action), not a refrain, and is held accordingly.

Close side: 40:16 ends on the decorative notice “וְאֶל אַ֖יִל תִּמֹרִֽים” ‘and on the post, palm trees’ -- a content close, not a refrain -- immediately before 40:17's transport verb “וַיְבִיאֵ֗נִי” moves the scene to a new location, the outer court. Close side: 40:19's “וַיָּ֣מָד” ... “מֵאָ֣ה אַמָּ֑ה הַקָּדִ֖ים וְהַצָּפֽוֹן” measures the distance from the lower gate's front to the inner court, ‘a hundred cubits ... east and north’ -- a summary figure that closes the general-court description before 40:20 pivots to a specific, named gate ('the gate of the outer court that faces toward the north'). boundary_rationale: Onset side: 40:20 names the outer court's north gate and measures it, “מָדַ֥ד אָרְכּ֖וֹ וְרָחְבּֽוֹ” ‘he measured its length and its width’, opening the run of five paired gate-descriptions (outer north 20-23, outer south 24-27, inner south 28-31, inner east 32-34, inner north 35-37) that carries the book's densest K/Q cluster: ten doubled-note verses at 40:21, 22, 24, 26, 29, 31, 33, 34, 36, 37, checked individually below. A transport verb sits inside this span at 40:24 ('he led me toward the south'), 40:28 ('he brought me to the inner court') and 40:32, which on the general granularity rule for this survey (a transport verb cuts) could argue for splitting outer-court gates from inner-court gates at 40:28. That alternative is weighed and set aside here because the gate circuit as a whole is bound by the repeated cross-reference formula 'according to these measurements' tying every named gate from 40:21 through 40:37 back to the dimensions fixed at the first gate, and treating that recurring cross-reference as one non-cut list rather than fragmenting it on its internal transport verbs is the more defensible reading. Close side: 40:37 ends the north inner gate on the shared refrain “וּשְׁמֹנֶ֥ה מַעֲל֖וֹת מעלו” ‘and eight steps, its ascent’, worded identically to the close of 40:31 and 40:34, immediately before 40:38's chamber-and-table description begins without any transport verb of its own -- a much weaker seam than any inside this row, which is why the cut is placed there rather than earlier.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: this is the weakest-evidenced internal seam in the part. 40:38 opens “וְלִשְׁכָּ֣ה וּפִתְחָ֔הּ בְּאֵילִ֖ים הַשְּׁעָרִ֑ים” ‘and a chamber, with its door, was by the posts of the gates’ with a bare vav, no transport verb and no measuring verb -- the topic shifts from gate architecture to the functional furniture used for slaughtering and washing the sacrifices, but nothing in the bytes marks the shift as a formula onset; it rests on content alone, following directly on the north inner gate's close at 40:37. The row continues through the singers' and priests' chambers (40:44-46, including the Zadokite priestly qualification, case-law texture inside a measurement row, disclosed) and closes at 40:47's “וְהַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לִפְנֵ֥י הַבָּֽיִת” ‘the altar was before the house’, a summary notice before 40:48's transport verb moves the tour into the temple building itself. A second transport verb follows at 41:1, “וַיְבִיאֵ֖נִי אֶל הַהֵיכָ֑ל” ‘he brought me to the nave... and measured’, disclosed here as continuous forward motion through one threshold sequence rather than a fresh row seam, since no formula or refrain close intervenes between the porch and the nave. The two-verse porch description (40:48-49) is held with the four-verse nave description (41:1-4) as one row rather than left as an under-three-verse fragment. boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:15 opens with the completion notice “וְכִלָּ֗ה” ‘when he had finished’ ... Four cardinal-direction measurements follow (east 42:16, north 42:17, south 42:18, west 42:19), each opening with a measure verb on its own line, then a summary at 42:20. Close side: 42:20 ends on the wall's purpose, “לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹֽל” ‘to make a separation between the holy and the common’ -- a genuine thematic close, and the point at which the whole measuring circuit that opened at 40:5 ends, immediately before 43:1's transport verb and the glory's return open a new kind of scene. Both sides of this seam are unusually well aligned for this part: a completion-formula onset and a purpose-clause close on one side, a transport-plus-glory onset on the other.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:1's transport verb opens “וַיּוֹלִכֵ֖נִי אֶל הַשָּׁ֑עַר” ‘he led me to the gate’, beginning the named hard seam behind the closed measuring circuit, and the row immediately carries the glory-of-YHWH device twice (43:4, 43:5), part of the book's nine-verse departure/return arc for that idiom, alongside the river-Chebar inclusio at 43:3 (one of eight such verses tying this scene back to Ezek 1 and 10) and 'I fell on my face' (one of five). The row turns from vision report to direct address at 43:6-9: a voice from the house, the man beside the prophet, the 'son of man' charge naming YHWH's throne and footstool, and the polemic against the house of Israel's defilement of the sanctuary by royal corpses and high places. Close side: 43:9 ends the divine resolution “וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכָ֖ם לְעוֹלָֽם” ‘then I will dwell among them forever’ immediately before the samekh recorded on this verse -- the first Masoretic paragraph mark anywhere in this part, ending a 103-verse unmarked stretch that has run since the pe behind 39:29. This is the only row in the part whose close carries genuine parashah corroboration, and it is disclosed as single-witness even so.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:10 opens “אַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם” ‘you, son of man’ directly after the samekh closing the prior row -- a near-form of the book's twenty-three-verse 'and you, son of man' sub-onset family, here without the leading vav, disclosed as such rather than counted against that sweep. It charges the prophet to show the house's pattern so Israel may be ashamed of its iniquities. Close side: 43:12 closes on a doubled envelope formula, “זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת” ... “הִנֵּה זֹ֖את תּוֹרַ֥ת הַבָּֽיִת” ‘this is the law of the house ... behold, this is the law of the house’, repeating the title at the top and bottom of the same verse -- one of the strongest lexical close-devices in the part, and the reason this three-verse span is held as its own row despite its length: the inclusio is a self-contained frame around 43:10-12 that a larger row would have to break through rather than around.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:13 opens with an explicit topic header, “וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙” ‘and these are the measurements of the altar’, functioning as a list-onset in the same way such headers do elsewhere in the book, immediately after the doubled inclusio that closes 43:12. The row descends through the altar's base, lower and greater ledges, hearth and horns, in cubit-and-handbreadth units, one of which (43:15) carries both an OSHB anomalous-form note and a K/Q note on the same word, disclosed together. Close side: 43:17 ends with the steps 'toward the east' before 43:18 opens with the messenger formula, a clean tier-1 onset on the far side even though this row's own close, like most others in the part, rests on content completion rather than a refrain.

boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:18 opens with “בֶּן אָדָם֙ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה” ‘son of man, thus says the Lord YHWH’ -- one of the book's 122 messenger-formula verses, and the clearest speech-onset in the whole part after the throne declaration of 43:1-9 -- introducing the altar's dedication ordinances. The utterance formula “נְאֻ֛ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה” appears mid-unit at 43:19, read as paragraph-final rather than row-final since the seven-day consecration instructions continue without interruption. The row carries the young-bull sin offering, the blood rite on the horns and corners, the second-day goat, the seven-day consecration, and closes at 43:27 on the same utterance formula, “וְרָצִ֣אתִי אֶתְכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה” ‘then I will accept you, says the Lord YHWH’, this time genuinely row-final. Close side: immediately after that utterance the verse carries two consecutive samekh marks -- the only doubled parashah mark anywhere in the book -- making 43:27 the best-attested close in the entire part and, since it is also the part's own boundary, the strongest evidence available for ending the assignment exactly here. Both sides converge unusually cleanly for this flagged region: a messenger-formula onset opposite an utterance-plus-doubled-mark close.
